row.title: A stack of slices lands one at a time, and a main-side red is proved on main before it is fixed
row.body: Ten bounded slices carried round two onto a main that kept moving, each built on the main that had just merged the one before it. Evidence, observed live on GitHub: #2815, #2819, #2825, #2827, #2828, #2829, #2830, #2838, #2839 and #2843 merged in that order and each deployed through the handoff lane. Two reds on main surfaced on the way (the JavaScript substance classifier missing a generated path; an invented-number test whose figure had become a measured value); each was reproduced on a clean main checkout and then fixed at its cause in the slice that met it. A CI step stopped by the actions budget or a GitHub rate limit is not a test failure: it got one re-run after the same suite passed locally, and it cleared. Verified by shipplan --check, which now reads: every entry has landed.

title: A stack of slices lands one at a time, and a main-side red is proved on main before it is fixed
